_doc: One entry per deviation shape. Lifecycle and gating rules: docs/GATING.md. Never delete entries; never flip still_reproduces without a fresh verifying scan.

entries.verdict: galaxyscope.py ~2145 ('THE CONTEXTUAL BASELINE FIX'): a file imported by others (popularity > 0) has orphaned_logic converted into api before recording. Micro-repro: 2-def file imported by a sibling records api=4, un-imported records api=2. With the spec's main->a->b->c chain and uncalled probes, api = defs x 2 in a/b/c, defs in main. Deliberate scoring semantics; raw counts unrecoverable from the DB (filed squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2536 asking for raw recording).

Keywords inside one string literal ('if eval fails, try open') count toward branch (+2), safety (+1), io (+1) but eval does NOT count toward high_risk_execution (routes to sec_tainted_injection instead). Micro-repro: identical files differing only in literal content, scanned end-to-end. Comments are fully stripped (verified 0 contribution); strings are inconsistently half-counted. 2026-08-31 cross-language extension: javascript reproduces python exactly (same decoy sentence, if/try count, eval does not); cobol does NOT shield at all (ALTER counts high_risk_execution from inside a DISPLAY literal) — the shielding is lexical-family-dependent, i.e. itself a language bias. 2026-08-31 legacy batch: fortran/ada/assembly count literals like cobol (fortran IF+GOTO+OPEN all count; ada 'if' counts; asm jmp/syscall count, and ARM's single-letter 'b' mnemonic even matches the filename inside %include "b.asm"); abap is a THIRD profile — shields branch/high_risk/io but NOT safety (TRY in a literal counts safety, isolated by micro-repro with comment-only vs string-only files). Worst amplification: a branch keyword inside a literal creates phantom branch context that triples state_mutation via the flux weighting (see state-flux-branch-weighting). Current behavior baked into manifests; whether intentional is the upstream question. 2026-08-31 batch 3 (12 mainstream languages): the selective profile (high-risk family shielded, branch/safety/io count) holds for c/cpp/csharp/java/go/kotlin/typescript/php/lua/swift; ruby counts eval from the literal (eval-as-bypass, like shell); perl's eval survives only because its bypass rule requires eval-followed-by-quote/paren (syntax shielding, not surface shielding); swift's api rule counts the word 'open' inside the literal (API-exposure mass from prose). try counts branch in csharp/java/kotlin/php/perl/swift/typescript. Swift's bare-open api FP filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2544. 2026-08-31 batch 4 (Tier-1 completion): a FOURTH profile — scheme's sexp-anchored branch keywords shield strings by SYNTAX (bare 'if' in a literal cannot match the paren-anchored rule) while its unanchored eval still counts; m4 is fully inert by the same mechanism (macro-name keywords). matlab and tcl join shell/ruby in counting eval-as-bypass from literals. dockerfile/makefile/livecode count literals wholesale. swift-open-style api hit not repeated elsewhere.

python's test rule includes \bassert\b and the safety rule includes assert: one planted assert counts both. Legitimate overlapping taxonomies; record +1 test wherever a safety assert is planted. Also c (bare assert( in both rules) and perl (ok( in the test rule alongside croak/confess safety plants).
python-family io rule matches the os./sys. prefixes that the globals plants (os.environ, sys.argv) necessarily carry: +2 io in whichever file hosts probe_globals.

Debt rules are whole-text, not comment-anchored, and '-' is a regex word boundary: HACK-LEVEL (data item, 2 code occurrences) counts fragile_debt, PROBE-TODO (paragraph name) counts planned_debt. Python's HACK_LEVEL is inert only because '_' is a word character — tokenization luck, not surface anchoring. Real-world FP shapes: COBOL BUG-COUNT/WS-FIX-FLAG, css .bug-icon, lisp fix-me. Filed upstream; observed counts baked into cobol manifest until fixed. Batch 4: scheme reproduces it — (define (probe-todo ...)) records planned_debt 2 (comment + identifier), confirming the lisp-family exposure predicted in #2537.

A bare token + period in Area B (CEE3DMP. / CEEMOUT., column 12) is counted as a paragraph header: func_start regex's post-sequence-area [ \t]* tolerates any indentation (relaxed/free-format support). By strict reference format a paragraph-name must start in Area A. b.cpy records func_start 5 (3 real paragraphs + 2). Whether the relaxed tolerance is deliberate is the upstream question. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2552 (closes #2538 -- func_start no longer mistakes LE service calls for paragraphs). Fresh verifying scan (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2552/#2611): b.cpy func_start 5->3, api 5->3 (orphan conversion follows), telemetry/safety_bypasses/state_mutation unchanged at 2/2/2 -- only the two bare-token FPs vanished. Manifest re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4. Surfaced by the first all-language CI run since #2552 merged (rosetta PR #5, which touches no data/ so the gate ran all 46).

'with (shape) {}' is parsed as a function named 'with' by the identifier(args){ alternation: the keyword exclusion list has if/for/while/switch/catch/return but not with. finditer-confirmed; switch (flag) {} in the same corpus is correctly excluded. b.js records func_start/args 4 for 3 functions.

cobol globals pattern includes WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION as an alternative — every fixed-format program with a working-storage section records globals >= 1. keyword_menu.py missed it (multi-word alternation; the miner only validates single-token candidates) — menu-tool improvement noted. main.cbl globals 1 baked in.

Token signals match ordinary identifiers that happen to spell a keyword: js probeIo's parameter named 'path' counts io +1 (path is a js io keyword). Inherent to keyword-based signals. Authoring guidance: avoid naming identifiers after menu keywords unless the collision is the point; record it when unavoidable.

state_mutation is recorded x3 when branch context exists in the file ('flux' semantics, matching the state_flux column name). Micro-repro: one := inside a real ada if -> 3; one := with no branch -> 1; the multiplier applies file-wide to all mutations. python/cobol corpus files were exact only because their b files had no branch context. Consequence of #2535: a branch keyword inside a string literal creates PHANTOM branch context and triples unrelated real mutations ('while' in a string: 2 raw := -> 6). REFINED (batch 3, go micro-evidence): the x3 weighting is PER-FUNCTION, not per-file — go b.go records 11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 (its own string carries the branch keyword) + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1 (no branch context in that function). Reproduces in all 12 batch-3 languages whose state rules have raw hits alongside the string decoy. Batch 4 adds the three cleanest per-function proofs: matlab main = 12 = one function's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1; powershell c stays x1 because probe_debt has no return/branch while its sibling does; dockerfile scopes flux per RUN instruction (4 = 1x3 + 1x1).

'USE A' does not resolve to a.f90 in the dependency DAG (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires); 'USE a' resolves. Fortran is case-insensitive, the suffix-map lookup is not. Corpus lowercased its USE targets to keep the DAG probe live; real uppercase legacy fortran (very common) silently loses its dependency graph.

ada's closing 'end if' re-matches \bif\b: every well-formed if statement counts branch at least twice (if + end if). Same class would apply to fortran 'END IF' spelled with a space (corpus used ENDIF, which is inert). Inherent to token-based branch counting on block-closed languages; baked in (main.adb branch 4).
GOTO is in both fortran's branch rule and its high_risk_execution rule — one planted GOTO counts both. finditer-confirmed.

assembly's branch rule includes call and ret (all control transfers) — correct for asm morphology but it means every probe body's ret and every glue call counts branch (main.asm: 10 = 3 call + 4 ret + 3 planted jumps). Cross-language branch comparisons must expect asm to run structurally hot.

ARM's single-letter 'b' branch mnemonic matches the word b anywhere literals count — including the filename inside %include "b.asm" (a.asm branch +1, finditer-confirmed). Any asm file mentioning a bare 'b' in a string/path gains branch mass. Sub-case of #2535's literal counting; not filed separately.

Top-level value bindings (CAFs like 'region = unsafePerformIO ...') count func_start/args like any function binding — morphologically correct for haskell, where top-level values ARE nullary functions. a.hs records 5 (3 probes + 2 planted globals). Type-signature + binding pairs count once, not twice (verified).
finally is in both haskell's cleanup and safety rules (finditer-confirmed on c.hs) — one planted finally counts both.

shell's branch rule counts the test brackets [ and ] as branch tokens (finditer on main.sh: if,[,],then,fi = 5 for one conditional) — every bracketed test costs +2 branch on top of if/then/fi. Defensible ([ is the test builtin) but a strong per-language inflation for cross-language branch comparisons.

'trap : TERM' counts globals: the TERM signal name collides with the TERM env-var keyword in shell's globals rule (a.sh globals 3 for 2 planted). Any trap handler naming TERM/USER-adjacent signals inherits this.

On languages without a same-file call graph the orphan census includes non-function shapes, so the orphan->api conversion count diverges from visible function counts: shell a/b convert 4 with 3 functions (the extra tracks the source line), sqlite converts 2/4/3 with 3 CREATE INDEX each and main.sql records orphaned_logic 7 for 4 indexes. Recorded as observed; gitgalaxy#2536 (raw hit_vector recording) would make these auditable.
^.read counts BOTH import and io (finditer-confirmed) — every corpus chain link adds +1 io in sqlite. By design (a .read is file io), but a cross-language io comparison must expect it.
GalaxyScope's census enumerates git-tracked files only; an untracked folder scans as '0 files mapped' with no per-file warning. Authoring workflow requires commit-before-verify (SPEC.md).

The <?php open tag's ? matches php's branch rule bare ternary-? alternation (finditer-confirmed): EVERY php file records branch >= 1 from its own open tag. A systematic per-file +1 on all real-world PHP; worth an upstream look at excluding ?> / <? tag context from the ? alternation.

kotlin's branch rule counts return: every file's branch = returns + real branch keywords (main.kt 8 = 5 returns + if/else/when; files with only returns record branch 3). Same cross-language-inflation class as assembly's call/ret. Batch 4: apex, objective-c, powershell, and zig (pattern-confirmed) also count return — it is a 5-language family, not a kotlin quirk; scala/dart/groovy siblings do not. Strengthens #2545's inconsistency framing. Batch 5: solidity is the 6th member (main branch 8 = 5 returns + 3 keywords).

kotlin's object declaration is the globals plant AND counts class_start (a.kt class_start 2) — a documented tier-1 exception to the no-classes tripwire, like cobol's PROGRAM-ID: object IS kotlin's singleton-class construct.

swift's _dependency_capture requires module names of 2+ characters ([a-zA-Z_][\w.]+), so 'import a' captures nothing: the corpus's swift chain never resolves, popularity stays 0, and no orphan->api conversion fires. Real single-letter modules are rare but the +-quantifier looks unintentional next to other languages' * shapes.

go's safety_bypasses rule's dot-import alternation (\bimport\s+(?:\.[ \t]+)?") matches EVERY quoted import, not just dot-imports: +1 bypasses per importing file corpus-wide. The (?:\.[ \t]+)? being optional makes the dot-import detector fire on all imports.

Languages whose visibility IS a naming/declaration convention count it wholesale: go's encapsulation rule counts every lowercase top-level symbol (7-9 per corpus file), perl's counts every my declaration (3-4 per file). Correct morphology, but cross-language encapsulation comparisons must expect these to run structurally hot.

typescript's args rule counts statement-position call parens (describe(kit), expect(kit)) in addition to declaration params — a.ts args 5 for 3 declarations (finditer-confirmed). Plants that are bare calls contaminate args in ts. Batch 4: apex and groovy count statement-position calls the same way (main args 7 = 4 sigs + 3 dispatch calls); objective-c over-counts via selector-colon segments (related morphology, recorded per-manifest).

m4 and scheme have _dependency_capture = None: include()/(import ...) count the import signal but can never produce a DAG edge, so popularity stays 0 and orphans never convert, corpus-wide. Two whole languages invisible to network_risk_sensor by construction — worth an upstream note whether deliberate. Batch 5: yacc (#include counted, capture None) and markdown (no import rule at all) join — four registry languages structurally invisible to the DAG.

Classification is per-file with no folder-context bleed: a .py file without its own micropython marker (import machine etc.) classifies as plain python even when every sibling is embedded — verified via the DB language column, twice (machine.idle() alone was NOT a sufficient discriminator; import machine was). Also two rule-level divergences on byte-similar code: embedded io drops os./sys. (python counts them), and orphan->api conversion does not fire under embedded classification. UPDATE 2026-08-31: the no-conversion divergence was fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2548 (embedded_python never wired into Python-family indentation scoping — found independently by a tri-comparison sweep); orphan->api conversion now fires under embedded classification (api 6, verified by the CI gate's fresh scan against gitgalaxy main). The per-file classification and io-rule divergences still stand. First ledger entry re-baselined by an upstream fix — the GATING self-improvement loop closing end to end.

dart's and zig's globals rules match final/const/var initializations at ANY indentation — function-local declarations count as globals (dart b/c +1 each from local finals; zig b 2 from function-local vars). Other languages' globals rules are top-level-anchored; these two look unanchored by accident.

Collective entry for batch 4's finditer-confirmed dual-rule keywords, each detailed in its language's manifest notes: agc RESUME (cleanup+branch), livecode global (globals+bypasses) and throw (safety+branch) and then/end-if inflation, tcl source (import+io) and close (cleanup+io) and trap (safety+branch), dockerfile ENV (globals+state) and HEALTHCHECK (func+safety) and FROM (import+class_start), makefile clean-target (func+cleanup+api), matlab clear/clearvars (state+cleanup), m4 popdef (state+cleanup), apex Database.query (high_risk+bypasses), powershell trap/continue (branch duals).

html's func_start rule (<script>/<style> tags) never fires end-to-end: the polyglot splitter consumes the tags before html's rules run (micro-repro: <script>var x=1;</script> records the JS body's state signal on the html row but func 0; raw regex matches all 13 corpus tags, engine records 0). Rule passes direct-detector tests but is dead in production scans.

Collective entry for Tier-2 finditer/report-confirmed shapes, detailed per-manifest: css at-rules triple-count (func+branch, @supports also safety; args tracks @import url); jcl EXEC PGM= is high_risk per step (probes use EXEC <proc>), api appears only via orphan conversion (no api rule defined); yaml counts every name:/description: as doc and embeds shell inside run: strings; solidity SPDX line = ownership on every file; html meta author is dual doc+ownership.

Post-gitgalaxy#2610 (PR #2611: prism strips //* to the comment surface; jcl gains safety=COND=, safety_bypasses=COND=EVEN/ONLY, telemetry=MSGLEVEL=/MSGCLASS=, shared debt rules) the shell re-plants args 13 (PARM= per EXEC step), safety 2, safety_bypasses 2, telemetry 2, fragile/planned debt 1/1 -- all land exactly (report-confirmed 2026-08-31). Remaining zeros are intended morphology, not extraction gaps: cleanup deliberately has NO jcl rule because the honest idiom DISP=(...,DELETE) would double-count io's DISP= (decision recorded in gitgalaxy#2610); doc has no JCL doc-comment idiom distinct from //* comments; test has no JCL concept; globals has no scoped-vs-global distinction (JOBLIB/STEPLIB plants would inflate io + dependency_links). dependency_links 4 vs planted 3 = the DD DSN= capture on CORPUS.DATA -- deliberate blast-radius design (datasets ARE jcl dependencies), finditer-confirmed. comment_lines stays below median even with the comment surface live: JCL permits no blank lines and the metric (total_loc - coding_loc) counts other languages' blank-line style as comment mass. branch 3 / state_mutation 2 match planted intent exactly; their red/amber standing is inflation of the cross-language median by the #2545 return-in-branch family and #2546 flux weighting, and re-baselines when those land.
